summary: Fiscal cryptographic and secret-handling posture is mature. Tamper detection has TWO independent vectors: DB-layer immutability triggers (DELETE/UPDATE blocked on MySQL via SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000', on SQLite via RAISE ABORT) AND application-layer HMAC chain re-walk (verifyChain re-computes every row and returns the first tampered id). Even if a future GRANT slip-up allowed UPDATE on a single row, verifyChain detects it on the next sweep. HMAC algorithm is hash_hmac('sha256', prev_hash || canonical(payload), secret) — canonical JSON is deterministically sorted recursively (sortRecursive in AuditLogService.php:358-374, normalise in FiscalSealingService.php:70-85), JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE so encoding stable across PHP versions and locales. Verification uses hash_equals (timing-safe). Secret resolution has three independent assertion paths (AuditLogService::assertProductionSafe, ZReportService::assertProductionSafe, FiscalSealingService::assertProductionSafe) — all enforce: (a) APP_ENV=production rejects dev sentinels listed in config/fiscal.php:175-183 (7 sentinels including 'changeme'/'change-me'/'test'/'dev'/'secret' which catches the most common .env mistakes), (b) min length 32 chars. Per-branch override is supported via env FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET_BRANCH_N (AuditLogService.php:273) — allows future per-tenant rotation without code change. Production secret refusal is loud (RuntimeException with clear runbook reference to docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md) — refusing to forge an unsigned chain is the correct fail-loud-not-quiet pattern. 6-year retention is enforced at the migration layer (audit_logs down() throws in production line 70-76 + unique chain index migration line 57-62). Branch isolation: AuditLogService::write requires explicit branch_id (line 93-98 — rejects null with InvalidArgumentException, callers must pass branch_id=0 for system/CLI events or positive int for tenant chain). Without this guard, a null branch_id would fall through to lastHashFor(null) which has no WHERE clause and would poison whichever branch chain was latest (POS-9-H.2.3 / F-C5 — historical bug fixed). Audit log payload is JSON-encoded canonical with sort — injection vector is bounded: even if a caller passes hostile keys, sortRecursive + JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES preserve structure but the HMAC binds the entire serialised string, so altering one byte breaks the chain. Hash prefix in fiscal log (substr 0,12) avoids leaking full hash in SIEM but enables join-back via audit_log_id (AuditLogService.php:174). No PII leak in logs: payload itself is never logged, only shape (action, resource, resource_id, hash_prefix). The 'mode' field in chain failure log (line 555) records strict vs degraded for forensic timeline. RED-team observations are in security findings below.

verified_invariants.name: HMAC algorithm is cryptographically correct
verified_invariants.evidence: AuditLogService.php:237-243 + FiscalSealingService.php:11-38. Sha256 HMAC, deterministic canonical input, hash_equals comparison. No homemade crypto.

verified_invariants.name: Canonical JSON is deterministic
verified_invariants.evidence: AuditLogService.php:335-374 sortRecursive: list arrays preserve order (correct for ordered data like payments), assoc arrays sorted with ksort recursively. JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE stable across PHP 8.x + MySQL/SQLite.

verified_invariants.name: Three production-safe secret assertions are independent
verified_invariants.evidence: AuditLogService.php:303-327, ZReportService.php:702-726, FiscalSealingService.php:92-115. Each is the LAST line of defense for its own signing path. A bug in one cannot bypass the others.

verified_invariants.name: Branch isolation enforced at write entry
verified_invariants.evidence: AuditLogService.php:93-98 InvalidArgumentException on null branch_id. lastHashFor(null) at line 245 would still walk cross-branch in CLI scenarios — protected by the entry guard.

verified_invariants.name: 6-year retention is enforced at migration layer
verified_invariants.evidence: Migration 2026_04_22_000002 lines 70-76 + 2026_04_22_100000 lines 57-62. APP_ENV=production rollback throws RuntimeException — operator cannot accidentally drop the audit chain via `php artisan migrate:rollback`.

verified_invariants.name: Dual-chain operator tool exists with distinct exit codes
verified_invariants.evidence: FiscalVerifyChainCommand exit codes 0/1/2/3 — TAMPER (1) separated from INVALID args (2) separated from EXEC ERROR (3). Monitoring can route correctly: TAMPER → compliance, EXEC ERROR → ops.

verified_invariants.name: Daily cron sweeps every active branch
verified_invariants.evidence: Kernel.php:174-208 dailyAt 03:30 iterates Kernel::activeBranchIds (whereIn legacy 1, canonical 5), logs every non-zero exit on fiscal channel with structured event names. Aligned with daily archive 02:00 via shared activeBranchIds() helper.

red_team_findings.name: TRUNCATE bypass on prod DB if GRANT not revoked
red_team_findings.vector: A privileged DB user with TRUNCATE privilege on audit_logs or z_reports can wipe the entire chain in one statement. MySQL BEFORE DELETE triggers do NOT fire on TRUNCATE. Mitigation requires explicit REVOKE TRUNCATE on production DB user — this lives in deploy doc, NOT migrations.
red_team_findings.recommended_action: VERIFY docs/DEPLOY.md / docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md actually contains the REVOKE runbook AND that the production-applied GRANTs match. If runbook is missing or inconsistent → ESCALATE immediately.

red_team_findings.name: Unprivileged secret leak via env var enumeration
red_team_findings.vector: FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET + FISCAL_Z_REPORT_SECRET + per-branch overrides live in .env. Any process running as the app user can readenv. If the deploy bundle is shipped to a CI runner without secret scrubbing, the secret leaks. Standard Laravel hygiene applies.
red_team_findings.severity: MEDIUM — operational, not a code defect
red_team_findings.recommended_action: Document secret rotation runbook in docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md (already referenced in error messages); add CI step that fails on FISCAL_* env vars present in shipped artifacts.

red_team_findings.name: Chain genesis prev_hash is overridable via env
red_team_findings.vector: config/fiscal.php:54 FISCAL_GENESIS_PREV_HASH defaults to 64 zeros. A malicious deployer changing this AFTER the chain has rows would cause every verifyChain to fail with chain_break on the first row. NOT a tamper attack — denial-of-verification.
red_team_findings.severity: LOW — operational denial of service, not a forge
red_team_findings.recommended_action: Add an opening_branch_genesis(branch_id, prev_hash) audit row at branch creation so the genesis becomes a DB-stored constant. V1.1 only.

red_team_findings.name: Empty payload + identical action repeated could produce a deterministic prev_hash collision target
red_team_findings.vector: Hypothetical: if an attacker could inject an audit row with identical (action, payload) that the upstream service was about to write, both rows would hash identically — but UNIQUE(branch_id, prev_hash) rejects the second one. The retry mechanism at AuditLogService.php:187 re-reads the tail and computes a new prev_hash, so the second row's prev_hash differs.

red_team_findings.name: fiscal.kiosk_auto_allocate_sequence=false rollback could create silent NF525 gap
red_team_findings.vector: Config flag at config/fiscal.php:137-141 defaults true. A future operator who flips it to false (emergency rollback) reverts to M-08 Option B behaviour where kiosk-paid direct TPE orders may remain fiscally unsealed if no POS operator collects them. If the rollback is not reverted promptly, gaps accumulate silently.
red_team_findings.recommended_action: Add a daily monitor that asserts config('fiscal.kiosk_auto_allocate_sequence')=true in production and logs CRITICAL if not. V1.1.

red_team_findings.name: verifyChain on huge tables blocks for hours without progress reporting
red_team_findings.vector: AuditLogService::verifyChain uses ->cursor() over the whole branch. At 10M rows it could run hours. NOT a security vuln per se — but a tamper attacker could create a large legitimate audit volume to delay forensic verification.
red_team_findings.status: FiscalChainValidator bounded tail (500 rows) mitigates the under-lock case
red_team_findings.recommended_action: Add progress logging every 10k rows during the on-demand verifyChain (operator command path only). V1.1.

red_team_findings.name: ZReportService.verifyChain in degraded mode logs but does not throw
red_team_findings.vector: ZReportService.php:561-568 — strict=false (non-production default) returns the result array with valid=false but does NOT throw. The caller must check $result['valid']. If a caller forgets, tampering is logged but processing continues. The frozen FiscalVerifyChainCommand handler at FiscalVerifyChainCommand.php:151 correctly reads $zResult['valid']. Other callers (test code, future services) might not.
red_team_findings.severity: MEDIUM — API contract risk for future maintainers
red_team_findings.recommended_action: Add a callable invariant assertion in CI: 'every call to ZReportService::verifyChain($branchId, false) must check $result valid'. Or document in service-level README. V1.1.

structural_recommendations_v1_1.label: Verify TRUNCATE GRANT mitigation in deploy doc
structural_recommendations_v1_1.rationale: DBA-OBS-1 + SEC-RED-1 converge. The triggers are useless if TRUNCATE is allowed on the prod DB user. Verifying the runbook exists is read-only, mandatory before next prod deploy.
structural_recommendations_v1_1.effort: trivial (read docs/DEPLOY.md + docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md + verify production grants table)

structural_recommendations_v1_1.label: Add fiscal.kiosk_auto_allocate_sequence guard alert
structural_recommendations_v1_1.rationale: Defense in depth — flag any rollback to legacy M-08 Option B behaviour.
structural_recommendations_v1_1.frozen_impact: new daily cron in Kernel.php (not frozen).

structural_recommendations_v1_1.label: Add branch-genesis row to remove FISCAL_GENESIS_PREV_HASH env coupling
structural_recommendations_v1_1.rationale: SEC-RED-3 — make the genesis a DB constant created at branch creation rather than an env var.
structural_recommendations_v1_1.frozen_impact: service code change (not in frozen list — branch creation lives in BranchService).

specialist_verdict: GREEN at code level — fiscal cryptography + secret handling + branch isolation + retention are correctly implemented. ONE P0-AUDIT (operator verification): confirm TRUNCATE GRANT is revoked on prod DB user — without this, the immutability triggers are bypassable. ESCALATE if deploy doc cannot be confirmed.
